transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-30 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Anna Lee (Redwood AE); James Patel (Redwood SE); Ravi Singh (Redwood SE); Clara Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Maya Rios (Soleris Head of ML); Tom Alvarez (CTO); Ibrahim Khan (Infra); Jenny Park (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Soleris wants to run a pilot to validate quality and cost trade-offs for their smart support agent. Primary concerns: hallucination control, latency at peak traffic, data residency and KMS integration. Customer to provide golden prompt set and production snapshot; Redwood to provide benchmark harness and security artifacts.

[00:00:12] Anna Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, i'll run through the goals then hand over to james for the technical details.
[00:00:24] Tom Alvarez: thanks anna, just want to be explicit, our success is two fold: quality metrics for the assistant, and confidence it scales under our peaks.
[00:00:36] Maya Rios: yes and also we need a simple scoring rubric so product can accept the model outputs, right now manual review is too slow.
[00:00:49] James Patel: perfect. quick agenda: success criteria, golden prompt set, regression + hallucination checks, workload sizing, timeline, next steps. i'll cover the benchmark harness and expected artifacts.
[00:01:12] Ibrahim Khan: quick infra note — most of our traffic is routed through our VPC peering to a cloud region in us-east-1, and any pilot needs to respect data residency and our KMS for encrypting tokens at rest.
[00:01:28] Anna Lee: noted, data residency and KMS are common ask. we'll send our SOC2 pack and KMS integration notes after this call.
[00:01:44] Maya Rios: also curious about the dedicated vs hosted tradeoff — if we hit the latency SLOs can we still stay on hosted for the pilot?
[00:01:58] James Patel: yeah often customers start hosted with a private tenancy option; for strict predictability Dedicated helps but it depends on your p95 targets and token rate. we'll size both.
[00:02:18] Jenny Park: when you say 'size both' do you mean you'll propose GPU counts and concurrency?
[00:02:27] Ravi Singh: right, we'll propose a couple of configs — e.g. small baseline (2 gpus) for light load, and a production profile (8 gpus) for peak. these are example numbers; exact counts depend on quantization and seq length.
[00:02:45] Tom Alvarez: can you give us a concrete success criteria now? helps us align stakeholders.
[00:02:53] Anna Lee: top-level proposed success gates:
- Quality: weighted score >= 0.82 on golden set (see scoring below)
- Hallucination: < 2% of responses flagged as hallucinations on the regression set
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 250ms for the majority of prompts under pilot load profile
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens under $1.25 (pilot target)
[00:03:26] Maya Rios: that hallucination number seems aggressive — how are you defining hallucination?
[00:03:33] James Patel: good question — our approach is a two-step check: format and fact-safety. format checks are deterministic (regex/structural) for the expected output shape; fact-safety uses a combination of retrieval + model-based classifier plus human review of a sampled subset. we'll define false-positive tolerance.
[00:03:57] [00:04:00] Maya Rios: ok, good. on format — our product expects JSON with fields id, answer, confidence. hallucination often manifests as missing citations or invented entity ids.
[00:04:15] James Patel: we'll add structural checks into the regression suite. also we'll instrument a 'citation coverage' metric that checks whether the model included references when expected.
[00:04:30] Jenny Park: about golden prompts — we have templates for support resolution, upsell suggestions, and triage. what's your recommended size?
[00:04:39] Anna Lee: target at least 1,000 golden prompts across categories with stratified sampling: 50% common queries, 30% edge cases, 20% adversarial/hard cases. the golden prompts should include expected output labels where possible.
[00:04:58] Maya Rios: we can get that ready. we'll anonymize any PII.
[00:05:05] Anna Lee: perfect. James can speak to scoring.
[00:05:10] James Patel: scoring approach (high level):
- Each golden prompt gets a composite score = 0.5 * semantic correctness + 0.2 * format compliance + 0.2 * citation coverage + 0.1 * latency penalty (normalized).
- Semantic correctness is either human-labeled (preferred) or automated using embedding-similarity + thresholding for the pilot.
- We'll produce per-category precision/recall and an aggregate weighted score.
[00:05:48] Maya Rios: for semantic correctness would you accept our existing human labels? we have some internal labels but they aren't fully consistent.
[00:05:57] James Patel: yes we can ingest your labels; we'll map them to a common schema and run a calibration pass (small seed of double-labeled examples) to estimate label noise.
[00:06:12] Tom Alvarez: what about regression tests — how do you guarantee we don't regress week-to-week?
[00:06:20] Ravi Singh: regression plan: baseline run in week 1, continuous regression with nightly runs for the pilot using the same golden set plus new sampled live traffic. any drop > 3% absolute on the weighted score triggers an alert and rollback.
[00:06:38] Jenny Park: rollback to what — older model or fallback policy?
[00:06:42] James Patel: we support canary and automatic fallback to a lower-capacity but higher-stability variant. we can also pin to a previous model version.
[00:06:54] [00:07:00] Ibrahim Khan: on the load side, our current peak is ~120 QPS average with 400 concurrent active sessions, token distribution median 45 tokens per request, 95th percentile 260 tokens.
[00:07:15] Anna Lee: great detail, that helps. for pilot sizing we'll simulate a 1.5x peak buffer so tests will target ~180 QPS and 600 concurrent sessions to account for spikes.
[00:07:29] James Patel: benchmark harness will include: load generator (k6-based), request templates, tokenization mirroring, and KV-cache warmup for conversational flows. note, KV cache warming materially affects latency — we'll include both cold and warm scenarios.
[00:07:49] Maya Rios: what's KV cash?
[00:07:52] James Patel: oh sorry — KV cache, spelling slip; it's the key-value cache for context tokens used in streaming chat.
[00:07:59] Tom Alvarez: does Redwood support prefix caching across requests? we have a lot of repeated context in our flows.
[00:08:05] Ravi Singh: yes we support prefix and per-session KV caching; we'll discuss eviction policies in the pilot config.
[00:08:14] Anna Lee: security question: will pilot requests flow through our customer's VPC or via the hosted API?
[00:08:22] Ibrahim Khan: we prefer through VPC peering ideally.
[00:08:25] James Patel: we can do either — for VPC we offer a private deployment option that keeps inference inside your network and integrates with your KMS. hosted is easier to set up but requires managed connectors.
[00:08:38] Maya Rios: timeline? we told execs 4 weeks can you map the activities?
[00:08:45] Anna Lee: proposed 4-week sprint:
- Week 0 (prep, 3-5 days): security docs exchanged, sample data upload, golden prompt set delivered.
- Week 1 (baseline): run golden set baseline on candidate model(s) and build the regression suite.
- Week 2 (load test): run the 1.5x peak load with cold/warm cache scenarios, gather latency/cost metrics.
- Week 3 (refinement + regression): tune batching, quantization, routing; run nightly regression and start human review sample.
- Week 4 (final evaluation): produce report, go/no-go decision, and next steps for Dedicated or production onboarding.
[00:09:30] Jenny Park: sounds reasonable. approvals — we need a legal signoff for data flow before week 1.
[00:09:36] Anna Lee: understood. we'll include a compliance checklist in the security packet.
[00:09:42] [00:09:50] Maya Rios: for hallucination detection you mentioned a classifier — is it Redwood's classifier or do we need to run our own?
[00:09:57] James Patel: we have an optional model-based classifier and heuristics; for high risk flows we recommend human-in-the-loop for a sampled subset until classifier confidence is acceptable.
[00:10:11] Tom Alvarez: cost modelling — can you provide a rough compare of hosted vs dedicated for our QPS?
[00:10:17] Ravi Singh: we'll run cost projection as part of the benchmark deliverable. preliminary rule of thumb: if sustained peak > 150 QPS with long seq lengths, Dedicated often becomes cost-effective. we'll quantify in the report.
[00:10:32] Anna Lee: ok i want to call out a few non-functional requirements we logged: audit logs retention 1 year, token-level billing breakdown, RBAC for model deployments, SSO via SAML.
[00:10:48] Ibrahim Khan: we need support for customer-managed keys (CMK).
[00:10:52] James Patel: yes CMK via KMS/HSM is supported in the private deployment path; we'll send integration notes.
[00:10:59] [00:11:10] Jenny Park: one more — how will you grade open-ended responses for downstream product acceptance?
[00:11:16] James Patel: we'll provide a graded rubric and tooling to surface examples that fail specific checks (format, hallucination, low semantic similarity). you can then triage by category and assign for human remediation.
[00:11:30] Maya Rios: curious about regression cadence after pilot if we go to prod.
[00:11:34] Ravi Singh: production cadence is customizable — common pattern: nightly regression, weekly human sample checks, and monthly model retrain/refresh windows.
[00:11:49] Anna Lee: any competitors you're evaluating?
[00:11:52] Tom Alvarez: we're also talking to Anthropic and a systems vendor called InferenceCo.
[00:11:58] Anna Lee: helpful to know, we'll include a short section on differentiators in our follow-up.
[00:12:05] [00:12:20] James Patel: technical note — for hallucination metrics we recommend two measures:
1) hallucination incidence (fraction of responses with invented facts)
2) hallucination impact (how many responses require human edit to be used).
We'll capture both during the regression runs.
[00:12:45] Maya Rios: great. on the golden prompts, should we include adversarial attacks? e.g., intentionally ambiguous or trick prompts.
[00:12:54] James Patel: yes include adversarial and also edge-cases that mirror customer bugs. those get higher weight in the scoring.
[00:13:05] Jenny Park: about human labeling — will Redwood handle labeling for 1k prompts?
[00:13:10] Clara Nguyen: we can coordinate labeling with our partner labeling pool or accept your internal labels — we recommend a hybrid to speed up.
[00:13:20] Maya Rios: budget constraint — we have a small labeling budget for the pilot. we'll likely do 200 human-labeled seeds and use automated checks for the rest.
[00:13:29] Anna Lee: that works; we'll calibrate the automated scoring against the 200 human labels.
[00:13:36] [00:13:50] James Patel: sample deliverables we'll provide: benchmark harness repo (link in follow-up), regression test suite, nightly report template, final pilot report with cost/latency/quality matrices, and config suggestions for Dedicated vs hosted.
[00:14:06] Tom Alvarez: link to docs and where to upload the golden set?
[00:14:10] Anna Lee: we'll send a secure upload link in the follow-up with instructions and expected schema.
[00:14:18] Ibrahim Khan: any gotchas around tokenization mismatch? our preprocessor strips some punctuation and that changes token counts.
[00:14:26] Ravi Singh: good catch — we'll mirror your tokenizer and request preprocessing to avoid mismatch. please include your tokenizer code or a sample preprocessor.
[00:14:38] Maya Rios: okay timeline and approvals — we'll aim to deliver the golden set and token distribution CSV by 2027-04-01.
[00:14:47] Anna Lee: action items are captured and we'll follow up with links and the security packet by 2027-04-02.
[00:14:56] [00:15:10] Jenny Park: last question — how do you operationalize model rollouts post-pilot?
[00:15:16] James Patel: we support staged rollouts with canaries per route, automatic fallback on SLO violation, and A/B experiment hooks so you can measure product metrics alongside quality metrics.
[00:15:30] Tom Alvarez: ok thanks everyone. let's sync on concrete dates in the follow-up.
[00:15:35] Anna Lee: thanks all, bye.

Post-call notes:
- Shared artifacts: redwood/benchmarks/soleris-harness (private repo link to be sent), security packet (SOC2 + KMS notes), secure upload link for golden prompts.
- Benchmarks to run: golden-set baseline, cold vs warm KV-cache latency, 1.5x peak load test with concurrency profile, nightly regression runs.
- Scoring: composite weighted score (semantic/format/citation/latency).
- Timeline: target pilot start week of 2027-04-12 pending security/legal approvals.

Transcript end.
